It solves the inefficiency of processing pixels that no voxel footprint covers, particularly at shallow voxel levels where footprints are small fractions of cell sizes [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method solves inefficiency by processing only pixels covered by voxel footprints, specifically noting that at shallow voxel levels, footprints are small fractions of cell sizes. Source [S1] explicitly supports this by stating: 'At the first voxel levels a cell is about a pixel and a foliage footprint a fraction of its cell, so four in five voxels cover no pixel centre, and a brick's rectangle is mostly pixels no footprint covers.' It further explains that the new technique processes 'voxels are splatted to the pixels their footprints cover, instead of every pixel of a brick's rectangle walking the brick's cells,' which directly addresses the inefficiency described in the claim.
